author: Jie Wang, David Jansen, Ir\'en\'ee Fr\'erot, Marc-Olivier Renou, Victor Magron, Antonio Ac\'{\i}n

difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition 4.1 (source0.tex lines 655--657, source label prop2), that in the moment relaxation for Heisenberg models there is no loss of generality in assuming that the dual functional ell vanishes on every word u whose signature eta(u) is not (1,1,1), delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 658--735 (78 lines, one adjacent proof environment). The proposition is the symmetry-reduction step on which the paper's scalable ground-state certification rests: it shows that a moment relaxation of a Heisenberg Hamiltonian can be block-diagonalised along the four signature classes of the Pauli-word basis, so that only the (1,1,1)-sector carries degrees of freedom. The proof is a genuine research-level construction: it assembles, for each of the four signature classes, the block matrices of the moment matrix, proves the equivalence of two flipped block positivity conditions through the article's auxiliary lemmas on block matrices with symmetric and skew-symmetric imaginary parts, and then transfers an arbitrary feasible dual functional to one supported on the (1,1,1)-sector while preserving the objective value by averaging over the symmetry group of the Hamiltonian. H2: a complete original research-paper proposition whose proof is a multi-step block-matrix and symmetry argument rather than a routine verification.
